name: cal_check
explanation: Tempester Voice, item 4: [routine] trusts the calibration page only when all 35 words were written (the Voice OS study §7.1, §10 row 10); otherwise the defaults, as DSI does for a blank page. DSI tests two words (A[1] and B[0] not 0xFFFF), so a half-written page is used. Here every word must hold what [routine] writes (tblwth.b 0xFF: upper byte 0xFF) and not the erased 0xFFFF. Nothing about the values: a code below [address] or a run that does not increase is used as DSI uses it ([routine], [address], does not bound the codes, and DSI's own default A[0] is low: a value test could reject a real page and detune the whole voice). Residual: a measured code of exactly 0xFFFF would be taken for an erased word (none on the six chips of the backup).

edits.why: rcall [address] ; W0 = 0 when every word was written
bra z,[address] ; load the 35 words (original path)
mov #0x1,W0 ; upper byte not 0xFF: not written by [routine]
